_schema_note: This is a REDACTED PUBLIC manifest. It intentionally omits internal authorship metadata (agent names, ticket IDs, private branch names) and reports rule changes at capability level, not exact pattern/matching mechanics. See ../../SECURITY.md for why. The full internal manifest (with exact detection-logic change notes) is not published.

noviscent_ai_sast.note: Base commit is Noviscent/AI-SAST's main branch at time of freeze. No rule files under the Noviscent detection packs were modified between this freeze and the capture of the three baseline runs.

secondary_scanner.amendment_note: Added after the first exploratory scan (a semgrep-only run, preserved under evidence/exploratory/ and marked NOT SCORED) showed zero SP001 findings. Inspection showed SP001 (Hardcoded Secret Detected) is implemented via gitleaks, not semgrep. Ground truth's predictions were written before any scan and already named SP001 as the expected rule for several scenarios, so adding gitleaks completes the intended scan surface rather than changing what was predicted. This amendment is disclosed here rather than silently folded in; all three scored runs (run1-run3) include both scanners.

content_sha256_method: sha256 of the concatenation of every *.yaml semgrep rule file and pack.json in the pack directory, in sorted path order: find <pack_dir> -type f \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name 'pack.json' \) | sort | xargs cat | sha256sum
packs_excluded_rationale: Out of scope for v0.1: these packs target SBOM/dependency-graph or compliance-baseline concerns, not the agentic/MCP code-level vulnerability classes exercised by DVAA and DVMCP.
scope_note: Damn Vulnerable LLM Agent (ReversecLabs) was reviewed as an optional secondary target but excluded from v0.1 to keep the benchmark within a one-week timebox and 12-20 scenario target; it is a candidate for a future round.

scanned_paths.exclusions_within_scanned_targets: Each DVMCP challenge also ships a server_sse.py that wraps the identical vulnerable logic in an SSE/FastAPI transport. It was excluded from the scanned path set because it duplicates the same vulnerable functions verbatim and would double-count identical findings without adding new ground-truth signal. This exclusion is declared here, not silently applied.

freeze_statement: Ground truth (ground-truth.csv) was written and committed to Noviscent's private source repository, from target source code and documentation review, BEFORE any Noviscent scan was executed against these targets. No Noviscent pack rule files were modified between this freeze and the capture of the three baseline runs. Because the private freeze commit is not itself public, an external reader cannot independently verify this chronology from public git history alone -- see REPRODUCIBILITY.md and provenance.md.

validation_rerun.semgrep_result: 43/43/43 unique findings -- exact finding-set match with the original pinned-version evidence (same 43 rule/relative-path/line tuples). Cross-version reproducibility confirmed across semgrep 1.163.0 -> 1.173.0.
validation_rerun.gitleaks_result: 29/29/29 unique findings -- within-version repeatability confirmed. Cross-version reproducibility NOT confirmed: gitleaks 8.30.1 vs 8.16.0 produced different finding sets (29 vs 36) due to different end-line offsets and aws-access-token detection. The original pinned-version evidence (36 findings) remains authoritative.
validation_rerun.notes: See evidence/validation-rerun-notes.md for full details. Scanner stdout/stderr logs from this validation re-run are under evidence/validation-rerun/, kept separate from evidence/raw/baseline/ to avoid false provenance. Original scanner stdout/stderr logs from the pinned-version run were not retained.
